## 22:07:15 (+20:15) — tc02 session EXPIRED: `idle_timeout`, ZERO inputs submitted — REAL DEFECT, NOT A FLAKE
- Evidence: `tc02/evidence/tc02-preflight-cleanup.json` (mtime 22:07:15) + live status: `state: finished, driver: stopped, guardian: clean, stop_reason: idle_timeout`, `next_sequence: 1` (no request sequence ever consumed = 0 inputs submitted).
- Mechanism (verified in code): `IDLE_TIMEOUT = 300.0` (5 min), `scripts/session_remote.py:35`; enforced at `:913` — kills the session when running + no active request + `now - last_activity >= 300`. `last_activity` is reset only when a driver REQUEST completes (`_request_worker`); status polls do not save it.
- What happened: the session started fine at 22:01:24, but the executor spent the next ~6 min studying the driver observe/act interface before submitting any input. The timer expired at ~22:06:24; cleanup recorded 22:07:15.
- Consequence: VS Code opened 22:07:56, AFTER the session was already dead — so no pill, no cursor change, no typing, `tc02/output/` empty. The user watched a dead overlay.
- FIX DECISION (user chose (a), 22:13): (a) PRIMARY — prepare EVERYTHING before start (study interface, open app windows), then start the session and send the first request within seconds; keep every gap between requests under 240 s. (b) SAFETY — if any deliberation gap approaches 240 s, submit a fresh observe as keep-alive (an observe is a driver request; it resets `last_activity` — verified in code). (c) NOT NEEDED — the 300 s timeout is a deliberate safety guard, not the defect; no Astra 6 report for the timeout itself. If (a)+(b) still fails, revisit (c).

## 04:50-04:54 (+6h20m-6h24m) - WORKER M: PAGE-SWITCH ROOT CAUSE PROVEN
- Driver fix: CDP read now fetches a compact in-page aggregate (keydown code counts, beforeinput types, composition count, ú/d keydowns) instead of the full event array. Byte oracle reads the auto-saved file, unaffected.
- page1-only control (fresh helper, only U+012F..U+015E): 47/48 correct; only the single page-1 char (U+015E) wrong, rendered as U+012F (its page-0 slot symbol). Base c0dhpP. Isolates the fault to the page switch itself.
- Debug build (/tmp/kbcorr-inspect/wtype-debug, dump hook only in the /tmp copy, never the repo): three keymap dumps produced, one per page (dump.0 1,921 bytes, dump.1 1,908, dump.2 348). All three VALID per `xkbcli compile-keymap --from-xkb --test`. Content exactly as designed: dump.0 maps XKB keycode 10 to Amacron (U+0100), dump.1 maps the same keycode 10 to iogonek (U+012F).
- 500 ms settle delay after the upload (debug build only): changes nothing, still 98 diffs, identical pattern. Not a timing race.
- Conclusion: on this stack (Hyprland 0.57.2), a virtual keyboard's keymap re-upload after the first one is not applied to the focused client. Only the first uploaded map ever takes effect. The spec's page-switch mechanism (PR 77's principle) does not work here for multi-page inputs. The shipped correction is correct and complete for every input fitting in one page (at most 47 distinct pool literals); the tc02 sentence uses about 20.

## 09:28:36 (+10:58) — 10x REVIEW SYNTHESIS (Astra lead + 3 Luna angles, all complete)
- Achieved times (judge-confirmed): tc02 t1 823 s, t2 140 s, t3 ~100 s; original tc02 1195.417 s; tc01 max in-session gap 223 s. Best achieved ~100 s (t3). 10x target ~10 s for a tc02-class task.
- 10x question: what would this look like 10x faster? What is the fundamental bottleneck? What if we rebuilt this part from zero?
- Findings (all four converge): the fundamental bottleneck is the serialized think-observe-think control loop / the between-request gaps, NOT the broker, transport, or observation pipeline. tc02-t1: 722.955 s between requests (87.8% of 823 s) vs 37.721 s broker request service (4.6%) and 1.8-2.1 s session start. Per-image observation cost only ~0.16 s (161.1 ms); per-keystroke >= 4 ms + 2R. Amdahl bound: making every local transaction free improves t3 only 1.15x; startup free only 1.02x.
- Most promising direction (converging): checkpointed scripts / local checked plans for known task shapes, batching deterministic actions, calling the strong model only when observed state deviates. Stress-S1 pattern already measured ~27 s/run vs 823 s for tc02-t1 (roughly 14-27x). Zero-rebuild sketch (laptop-side coordinator state machine, model returns plan JSON with checkpoints, images only at checkpoints) targets 30-55 s for tc02. Observation: ROI crops + reusing after-images can cut per-frame bytes 10x but cannot 10x wall time alone. Transport: batch 10+ actions per act + persistent broker stream is a control-plane 10x candidate; end-to-end 10x unproven.
- Corrections from the executor-time worker (verified against raw logs): tc02-t2 max gap is 20.993 s (not ~40 s), tc02-t3 is 11.834 s (not ~25 s), tc13 is 19.803 s (not 171 s); tc13's session lasted 2:01, not ~5 min. Honest limit: the logs cannot split the inter-request gap into model inference vs image reading vs SSH (no inference timestamps; the L3 helper runs session_remote.py locally).
- DECISIONS:
  - ADOPT: local checked plans / checkpointed scripts for known task shapes (replacing the stepwise model loop); selective observation (ROI crops + reuse after-images as checkpoints); local task execution (goal once, result once); deterministic execution with a model supervisor; expected window transitions as transactions (fixes tc01/tc05 action-success/capture-failure session deaths); state contracts instead of guessed sleeps; targeted instrumentation.
  - DEFER: screenshot-diff transport, persistent broker-client connection, native input throughput, smaller/faster model cascade (each with a stated trigger in the Astra review); batching alone (needs checkpointed plans to reach 10x); full plan before start (borderline ~76 s); compact state ledger.
  - REJECT: fully blind execution / a11y-only, indefinitely warm GUI lease, bypass input for tc02, concurrent input on the shared seat; session reuse across cases; optimizing start-to-ready alone; per-character 10x (unproven); caching observations/windows/focus; set_text, browser fill, direct writes, cu.py act bypasses; evdev/uinput without a contract change; faster/cheaper model alone (~4.7x optimistic ceiling); observation reuse; pre-prepared branches.
- This is a RESEARCH loop, not a mandate to rewrite now. The ADOPT items are proposals for the next implementation cycle, not implemented in this run. No code was changed by the 10x review.
- Sources: 10x-review-astra6.md (25,767 B), 10x-executor-time.md (17,122 B) + 10x-think-codex-report.md (28,162 B), 10x-observation.md (22,746 B) + 10x-observ-codex-report.md (28,622 B), 10x-transport.md (27,690 B) + 10x-transport-codex.md (38,316 B).

## 10:33 (+7m from cycle T0 10:26) - W-BATCH research complete: opt-batch-research.md

- Deliverable: `improvements/opt-batch-research.md` (51.6 KB). Research + design only, no code changes, no repo changes, no live tests. Verified against the real traces, not just the reviews: tc02-t3/t2/t1 request records on the laptop (read-only SSH), `/tmp/mp-l3.py`, `scripts/cu.py` (`desktop_act`, `validate_actions`, `keyboard_groups`, `settled_observation`).
- Ground truth established: tc02-t3 is 14 requests; seq 11 already proves a 3-action batch (click field + Ctrl+A + type path, completed 3/3, exec 510.7 ms); seq 12 already uses `--no-after` for the dialog-closing Save click. t2 differs by exactly one redundant request (`observe-after-path`). The 4 s menu settle is an executor-side recipe, not a broker sleep; no `wait` action exists in any t1/t2/t3 record.
- Design: local checked-plan controller (laptop-local, plan supplied once before `start`, zero model round trips on the happy path) + complete tc02 procedure spec P0-P1-G0-S1-S6 with preconditions, local checkpoints, and escalation triggers per step. Projected execution stopwatch ~6.2 s vs t3 ~100 s (budget table in the doc, with honest caveats: S2 500 ms wait is tunable, `windows` cost unmeasured).
- Batching rules: safe chains (click+type, select-all+type, click-menu+wait+click-validated-row, repeated types, keyboard nav of open menus, type+Enter) vs never-batch (anything branching on unseen state, anything crossing a window/dialog transition, type-then-Save in one batch, drag+follow-up, scroll+read-answer). Soft cap 8 actions per batch (hard cap 32 broker-enforced). Partial-batch failure protocol: never blindly replay; fresh observation, resume only the uncompleted suffix if preconditions still hold, else escalate; 1 retry per checkpoint max.
- After-image rules: adopt as next checkpoint only when same window/bounds/monitor/compositor, fresh under 90 s, expected change only; fresh observe still required on window/dialog transition, focus change, unexpected state, geometry change, any READ step, any checkpoint failure. Removes 2-3 standalone observes per tc02 (observe-menu, observe-after-path).
- Window transitions as transactions: 3 recorded outcomes (action completed; old surface gone as expected; successor bound+verified). Root cause verified in `cu.py`: `guard()` runs before/after every group bound to the ORIGINAL window, and the final after-capture targets the original window address, so a dialog close forces `ok: false` + `capture_error` even when all actions succeeded; `--no-after` skips the capture but not the trailing guard. Fix must parameterize guard + capture by expected terminal window together, with a distinct transition outcome in the envelope. A vanished window is never by itself proof of saving (needs title change + byte verification too).
- State contracts vs sleeps: full inventory (menu 4 s becomes in-batch wait 500 ms + dialog checkpoint; helper 0.5 s poll sleep becomes long-poll/push, 7-18 s/trial; 80 ms pre-capture sleep KEEP; S1 stress 14 s of sleeps become readiness polls; S4/S5 intentional sleeps KEEP; ms-scale holds KEEP).
- Supervisor: L1 deterministic local procedure, L2 bounded model decision (fixed packet, one named branch, no new procedures), L3 deliberative (only level that may rewrite the plan). Escalation triggers listed.
- Generalization table for all 13 cases: tc05 (same dialog, Omawrite Ctrl+L branch), tc13/tc03/tc10/tc06/tc04 (batch shapes), tc01 (tool grounding + dialog-close fix), tc08/tc11 (read steps stay L2), tc09 (cross-app copy/paste batches), tc07/tc12 (minimal batching, controller still removes model round trips).
- Implementation handoff (7 ordered items) + 3 open questions for Astra 6 (L2 placement, local pixel-region checks as checkpoint predicates, broker-version bump for the transition envelope). Deliberately NOT in this design: bypass input, concurrent input, warm-session reuse, blind execution, model cascade, screenshot-diff transport, persistent stream, native input work (all deferred with triggers, per the 10x review).

Conclusion: crops cut BYTES ~10-32x and encode 6-24x, but local capture time only ~1.4x (capture/decode near-fixed). Saving is paid 3x per act (preflight recapture + after-capture use the same crop, cu.py:1442,1603). The 10x-observation "plausibly 10x bytes" claim is now MEASURED.

  - a11y CANNOT give coordinates: grep for component/position/extents in a11y.py returns zero hits; describe() never calls the Component interface. a11y is semantic confirmation (pressed/checked/selected/editable/disabled) + native click for exposed controls only. Blind spots confirmed in code/record: GTK popup entries not exposed (tc04), VS Code EditContext uninformative, tree truncated at 80 items / 500 nodes / 2 s. set_text exists but stays PROHIBITED.
  - Layout caching is NOT observation caching (the latter stays REJECTED per the 10x synthesis). Cached item is relative geometry keyed by (app, version, window size, monitor scale), validated on every use by the existing guard() bounds/focus checks (free, already run) + a small verification crop. Stale-entry risk is real (tc01's 4 Rectangle Select misclicks are the shape of it); mitigation is verification crop on every use + two-strikes retirement + never acting from a prediction without a fresh crop behind it.
  - Coordinate prediction works only as "predict where to crop, verify with a fresh native crop, act from the crop". Fully blind prediction stays REJECTED (test-cases.md:33, Astra 4b).
  - Crops also reduce spurious preflight refusals: screen_changed global mean is computed over the crop only, so changes outside the crop no longer refuse the act; focus guard still catches focus changes.
  - Failure-mode map: crops + tool-state checks fix the tc01 pixel-accuracy class; they do NOT fix tc02 Save As loop (deliberation, not pixels), tc05 dialog semantics, or tc04 popups (keyboard nav). Dialog-close capture failure (tc01 lost 2 sessions) is untouched by crops; needs Astra (f1) transaction handling.
  - Per-app layout tables: YES for the 6-8 recurring suite surfaces, as relative geometry + verification rules + semantic notes (e.g. Omawrite Name takes a bare name, Ctrl+L focuses location; GTK popup items not pointer-clickable; Pinta tooltip may eat the first Ellipse click), keyed by version/size/scale, self-healing on verification failure.
- RECOMMENDED DESIGN (one): predict-then-verify-crop grounding inside the checkpointed local controller. Plan names controls by semantic identity; layout table predicts the crop region; fresh native crop verifies; act from the crop and batch within the state; after-image is the next checkpoint; a11y state check before dependent actions; expected window transitions are transactions; no blind clicks, no set_text, no observation caching.

## 16:20 (+4h53m) — G0 ROOT CAUSE FOUND (coordinator 2f320c0f, investigation 16:12-16:20, evidence from A1 controller log + session_remote.py + relay state)

- ROOT CAUSE: the running broker is STALE. The relay service (computer-use-relay.service, MainPID 106001) started Tue 2026-11-17 00:19:28 +07 and has NOT restarted since. The Step 1 long-poll change (commit d45434c, 11:28 17/11: `Broker._result` waits on `record.done` up to 120s) landed on disk AFTER the relay started, so the running process still executes the PRE-long-poll `_result`, which returns the record immediately without waiting. `session_remote.py` on disk last modified 11:59:28 17/11; relay still runs the 00:19-loaded code.
- Mechanism (matches the logs exactly): controller calls `result` ~0.15s after `request`. G0-windows is fast (~0.1s), so the record is already `completed` when `result` is called -> works. G0-observe takes ~0.3s (image capture + encode), so at `result` time the record is still `running`; the stale `_result` returns `{'ok': True, 'status': 'running'}` immediately (result CLI returncode 0, 0.2037s, NOT a 120s wait). The controller's `_driver_body` (tc02_controller.py:422) requires status in ('completed','failed','unknown') -> escalates. Both A1 and B1 failed identically at the same step: deterministic, not flaky.
- Ruled out by evidence: result call did NOT time out (0.2s, not 120s); the broker DID return (returncode 0, ok True); the record status was `running`, not an error envelope; `RequestRecord.status` defaults to 'running' and `done` is only set in `_request_worker` finally / the EOF path (both set a terminal status first), so no code path returns 'running' after a wait — the wait simply never happened in the running process.
- FIX (delegated next): (1) restart the relay safely when idle so it loads the current session_remote.py; verify with a live broker observe+result probe that `result` now returns terminal `completed`; (2) add a fail-closed stale-code guard in code so this class of bug cannot silently recur (broker reports its loaded-code hash in status; controller preflight compares with the on-disk file and escalates clearly on mismatch; and/or sync-installed.py restarts the relay when broker-loaded files change); (3) tests + full suite green, commit + push as phamTuan207 + sync; (4) rerun Gate A 3x + Gate B under the fixed lease contract (leases in ~/.cache/agent-computer-use/leases/<run-id>/, 0700 dirs, never /tmp). Geometry (floating editor exactly 901x1176) must not regress.
- Watchdog 7f6ae609 is running (started 16:14, polls every 5 min, restarts after 15 min stall).

## 18:23 (+07) — W1 DYNAMIC DONE (worker 60a4a04f)

- Owner order (18:19): research ONLY, web + VM. No laptop touched (no SSH/sessions/code/live tests). Never ydotool.
- Deliverable written 18:23: improvements/liquid-glass-best-w1-dynamic.md (38,192 bytes). Every claim cited with URL + access date 2026-11-17. No invented numbers or code.
- Research done 18:21-18:23: 8 web searches + 7 page reads (preetsuthar interactive demo, shayxo how-it-works / reference-measurements / measured-model / tab-bar, WWDC25 219 transcript, MacStories review, theatom docs, amir-abushanab showcase, MotionKit, react-native-glass-lens, Kyant0 walkthrough, AMNH refraction).
- Key findings:
  - Dynamic effect = fixed warp field x per-frame fresh backdrop. Content scrolling under glass goes stretch (2x) -> stationary seam -> mirrored upside down -> identity (shayxo foldSource). That sequence IS the glass-bottle feel; it needs no animation code.
  - No true parallax in Apple glass (single flat backdrop plane); parallax in recreations is authored decoration, not measured. Device-motion specular and Spatial Scenes are separate effects.
  - Timings verified: held lens forms <=66 ms (2 frames), subsides 330-460 ms (10-14 frames); form spring ~110 ms, subside ~330 ms (shayxo tab bar, authored fit); round button press ~170 ms in / ~200 ms out; cover-sheet fold past ~350 px pull = ~117 pt at 3x, consistent with the 117 dp figure, not a conflict.
  - Bend TRACKS backdrop motion with no lag term in any model; only shape/formation have springs. Velocity-coupled refraction exists only in third-party authored work (MotionKit springs, RN glass-lens stretch formula), never measured from Apple.
  - Hard question answered: a static pill CAN have dynamic quality (backdrop moves, compositor re-renders per frame, shadow/tint adapt as text scrolls under, per WWDC25 scroll edge effect), but it can NEVER have the fold, the held lens, the gel strain, or morphing. Apple's own resting indicator is NOT glass (flat, no refraction band). Judging a resting pill against the held lens is a category error.
  - Precedent that cuts both ways: @zakisheriff/liquid-glass and react-native-glass-lens both deliberately PAUSE refraction while scrolling (blur + rim carry the look in motion) for performance. If per-frame refraction is too expensive, that is a legitimate deliberate choice, not a failure.
  - Acceptance test proposed: slow-scroll VIDEO of text under the pill, frame by frame, looking for rim deformation. Stills cannot pass this, which is the trap the current work fell into.
- Gaps recorded in file section 6: no Apple velocity dependence, no parallax numbers, no Apple spring constants for glass, no scroll-speed readability threshold, no tilt-response measurement, shayxo reference recording not public.
- Note: MEMORY.md changed during this task (18:22 entry, Omarchy Agentic OS research coordinator 05b79337). Unrelated to W1; noted, not acted on.

The work is 0.2 ms out of 107.5 ms, 99.8 percent overhead. Recompile proven by strace: script mode opens the .py source twice and never touches the .pyc; import mode opens the .pyc once. Every invocation shape costs 105-111 ms, even --help and argparse errors.
- Prototype: faithful Rust replacement, std-only, zero crates, 374 KB stripped, clean build 7.5 s. Implements status/result/request with exact wire behavior (lease validation, safe file reads, generation checks, exit codes) and argparse-compatible help/errors including quirks. serve/start/finish parse identically but refuse execution (deliberate scope boundary, once per task not per step).
- Fidelity: 74/74 diff cases pass, 0 fail (live broker, no broker, fake broker, 8 lease shapes, 33 argparse cases, 100 KB response, unicode). Two documented divergences, both unreachable in controller use: non-canonical number lexemes (1e2 vs 100.0) and relative XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (Python crashes with traceback, Rust prints clean error JSON, same exit code).
- Before/after (n=31, interleaved, 0 mismatches): Python about 106-110 ms vs Rust about 1.7-2.6 ms on every path, saving about 104-107 ms per spawn (42-65x). One real bug caught by measuring: first JSON parser was quadratic on long strings (Rust 181 ms vs Python 109 ms on a 100 KB response); fixed to a linear fast run, now 2.64 ms.

H1 1974 s to about 1958 s (about 0.8%). Key caveat: this attacks the same about 3 s as the Step 3 persistent stream, it does not stack, and per request a persistent Python client (0.2-0.4 ms in-process) is actually faster than one-shot Rust (2.5 ms). The Rust binary wins on deployment risk (drop-in swap, no broker change), not on per-request speed.

## 2026-11-18 22:47 +07 - W-PA1 PRIOR-ART SURVEY DONE: speed-prior-art-latency.md (22:43:27 to 22:47:46 +07, 4m 19s wall)
- Worker: Luna 6 Max, read-only, no code changes, no plugin load, no logout or reboot, no ydotool. Google search first, then primary sources (arXiv papers, vendor docs) or close secondary summaries where marked SECONDARY.

- Headline findings: (1) reasoning-effort dial per step type is the top lever: max took 30.6s to first text vs 3.0s at low in one Oct 2026 test, 2,517 vs 56 reasoning tokens; accuracy peaks near 1,024 thinking tokens then reverses (Zhou et al., Apr 2026). (2) Observation masking halves agent cost and matches LLM summarization on solve rate (Lindenbauer, Aug 2025); observations are about 84% of turn tokens. (3) Rule router by step type: windows plus observe plus verify carry 19.3s of think and do not need max reasoning. (4) Prompt compression on short prompts is NEGATIVE: up to 18% end-to-end only above about 5k tokens, overhead cancels gains below that (Kummer et al., Apr 2026); independently confirms the synthesis log's NEGATIVE verdict. (5) Faster screenshots without a redraw guard made the agent SLOWER: env time down 8.72s, agent time up 18.20s (cua-speedrun, Sep 2026). (6) Speculative decoding can run at 0.44x baseline on the wrong model; measure acceptance first. (7) Prompt-caching open check: read one Codex usage record for cached-token fields; OpenAI auto-caches prefixes over 1,024 tokens.
- Section K lists 10 proven failures / do-not-redo items. Section L ranks 8 prototype candidates by expected think-time saving. Four source links I first drafted from memory were replaced with verbatim URLs returned by search before delivery.

## 2026-11-18 22:48 +07 - TRACK 2 PRIOR-ART SURVEY ANGLE 2 DONE (Luna 6 Max, grounding / observation / benchmarks)
- Started 22:43:34 +07, finished 22:48:23 +07. Elapsed 4m49s wall. Read-only survey, no code changes, no plugin load, no logout or reboot, no ydotool. User asleep, not disturbed.
- Deliverable: improvements/speed-prior-art-grounding.md (352 lines, 80,592 bytes, 0 em dash, 0 en dash, verified by grep).
- Method: Google first, primary sources read where reachable (arXiv HTML, project pages, model cards, leaderboards). About 30 sources with author/date, tried/measured/applies per entry, plus a ranked applicability table and a do-not-redo list.
- Headline findings: (1) OSWorld-Human is the pivot paper: planning plus reflection is 75 to 94 percent of latency, later steps up to 3x longer, best agents take 2.7 to 4.3x more steps than necessary; screenshot-only history does not help, only text history does. (2) Zoom/crop at inference time is the most replicated accuracy win: RegionFocus UI-TARS-72B Pro 38.1 to 50.2, ScreenSeeker OS-Atlas-7B 18.9 to 48.1, ZoomClick 61.4 to 73.1. (3) Best local grounder for the RTX 4050 6GB is Ferret-UI Lite 3B (Aug 2026): Pro 53.3, v2 91.6, OSWorld-G 61.2/55.3, beating UI-TARS-1.5-7B (49.6 Pro); UI-TARS-1.5-2B second. 7B grounders borderline on 6GB, CogAgent hard NO (29GB VRAM at BF16). (4) CLI beats GUI on steps: 10.7 vs 18.6 steps (Gu et al. 2026), independent support for code-execution-as-action. (5) OSWorld-Verified top 90.19 percent (Jul 2026) and AndroidWorld archived saturated at 100 percent self-reported (Nov 2026); OSWorld 2.0 is the current hard test at 44.33 percent binary (Oct 2026 board).
- Do-not-redo flags added: full a11y-tree dumps (5,000 to 15,000 tokens, worse than screenshot), a11y-only grounding, blind execution, pixel/observation caching, visual token merging/pooling (ShowUI ablation 70.8 to 42.3), CogAgent locally, Rust harness rewrite (Track 1 stay-Python verdict).
- Flags needing verification before the prototype plan re-ranks on them: BiGrounder-4B end-to-end numbers (72.4 AndroidWorld, 42.8 OSWorld) are single-source and far above all other grounder-plus-planner results; FSP 10 to 13x token reduction is a projection, not a measurement; Ferret-UI Lite OSWorld-G is 61.2 in its abstract vs 55.3 in its body table; no local model was loaded in this survey, so 6GB VRAM fit is a size judgment, not a measured load test.
- Next: merger worker folds the 3 survey files into improvements/speed-prior-art.md and re-ranks the prototype plan by think time, then prototype workers launch.
